handoffs.message: Repaired the reviewed loss window; PR #4211 head eb52a3b0f with all three required checks green. The prior rejection was correct and its reproduction is now a test. Single-phase admission is replaced by a two-phase leased fenced reservation in services/telemetry/ingest_svc.py: begin() takes a reserved claim with an owner token and lease; a committed record is written only after the durable enqueue receipt and only a committed record makes a retry an idempotent 202 duplicate; a caller meeting a live reservation gets 503 INFRA_ADMISSION_IN_FLIGHT and must retry, never 202; commit() and release() are token-scoped so an owner whose lease was taken over is fenced out of both; an expired reservation left by a crashed replica is recovered by the next caller with a fresh token; and cancellation or a buffer error releases the claim instead of stranding it. New tests: two-replica loser-must-retry against a stalled enqueue, four concurrent replica processes where exactly one commits and every loser gets in_flight, SIGKILL of a real service instance inside the enqueue window then lease-expiry recovery, fenced commit/release after takeover, and release on cancelled enqueue. Reinstating the exact reviewed bug fails 3 of them. 33 focused tests and 309 telemetry tests pass, with the one pre-existing PANTHEON_RUNTIME_MANAGER_URL-dependent lineage failure reproducing on the unmodified tree. Evidence re-cut at docs/deployment/evidence/twelve-loop-gap/OPS-L12-BFF-INFRA-TELEMETRY-AUTHORITY-001/evidence.json with your rejection as record_log sequence 2, refreshed checksum, and a new HTTP readback showing the in-flight refusal, the duplicate only after the receipt commits, crash-reservation recovery, and zero orphan reservations. Auto-merge is disabled pending your decision. AC6 remains pending_reviewer.

Re-review PR #4211 head 4e24e895f: the durability rejection of head 0d0b015c9 is repaired. Infrastructure health admission now fails closed with 503 INFRA_BUFFER_NOT_DURABLE before the reservation and again before the commit, using the buffer's own is_durable() as the sole authority, so no volatile enqueue can ever be committed; a volatile deployment writes zero ledger records and /healthz reports infrastructure_health_buffer_durable=0. Added a real process crash matrix (crash before put, after durable put before commit, after commit, restart replay, four-process replica concurrency) asserting no false success and no permanent loss, plus durability-authority tests including one proving no PANTHEON_* environment variable can enable volatile admission. Tests inject a file-backed fsync broker double defined in the test module that buffer.create_buffer cannot select, and injecting a volatile buffer through the same in-process seam still fails closed. Evidence re-cut against a REAL NATS JetStream file-storage work queue: the admitted event is still in the stream after the telemetry process is SIGKILLed and the restart replay answers duplicate; the memory-buffer readback residual is retired. Verified: pytest services/telemetry/test_infrastructure_health_ingest.py 44 passed; pytest services/telemetry 320 passed with one pre-existing PANTHEON_RUNTIME_MANAGER_URL failure reproducing on base 0d0b015c9; mutation controls fail 5, 1, and 8 tests respectively, the last including all three crash-window tests. No config change, no weakening of strict auth or trading validation. Review file: docs/deployment/evidence/twelve-loop-gap/OPS-L12-BFF-INFRA-TELEMETRY-AUTHORITY-001/evidence.json
